I've now viewed 12 reference images. Let me analyze my findings:

**Test image features:**
- Opened soybean pod showing seeds inside
- White/gray cottony/crusty material on the seeds inside the pod
- Seeds appear dull, discolored (dark brownish + white mixed)
- No clear external pod lesions visible

**Comparison with candidates:**

- **Downy_mildew**: Description specifically says "no external pod symptoms; interior of pod and seed covered with dried, crusty, whitish fungal mass containing spores; seeds appear dull white" — this directly matches what's shown: white material INSIDE the pod on the seeds
- **White_Mold**: Seeds "white and cottony; may be replaced by sclerotia" — reference images showed external fluffy white mycelium on stems, not internal pod symptoms
- **Phomopsis**: Reference showed dark pycnidia lesions on pod exterior, chalky white mold on seeds — test image doesn't show the characteristic pycnidia patterns on pod walls

The **Downy mildew** description is the only one that specifically describes white/grayish fungal mass INSIDE the pod on the seeds with no external pod symptoms — which exactly matches the test image showing the pod interior filled with white/gray material on the seeds.
